claims.nodeLabel: NASA Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Independent Study Team Report
claims.text: On data quality: 'At present, the detection of UAP is often serendipitous, captured by sensors that were not designed or calibrated for this purpose, and which lack comprehensive metadata. Coupled with incomplete data archiving and curation, this means that the origin of numerous UAP remain uncertain.'

claims.text: Cover: 'NASA / UNIDENTIFIED ANOMALOUS PHENOMENA / Independent Study Team Report'. 36 pages, PDF CreationDate 13 September 2023 21:27 UTC; publicly released 14 September 2023.

claims.nodeLabel: NASA Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Independent Study Team Report
claims.text: Following the report, 'NASA's Science Mission Directorate' named 'a Director of UAP Research to centralize communications and leverage' agency expertise.

claims.nodeLabel: NASA Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Independent Study Team Report
claims.text: Core recommendation: 'We recommend that NASA play a prominent role in the whole-of-government effort to understand UAP by leveraging its extensive expertise to contribute to a comprehensive, evidence-based approach that is rooted in the scientific method. We specifically recommend that NASA utilize its existing and planned Earth-observing assets to probe the local environmental conditions associated with UAP that are initially detected by other means.'

claims.nodeLabel: NASA Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Independent Study Team Report
claims.text: On extraterrestrial origin: 'To date, in the peer-reviewed scientific literature, there is no conclusive evidence suggesting an extraterrestrial' origin for UAP. The panel nonetheless frames the question as legitimate: 'There is an intellectual continuum between hypothesizing that faraway extraterrestrial civilizations might produce detectable technologies, and looking for those technologies closer to home.'

claims.nodeLabel: NASA Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Independent Study Team Report
claims.text: On stigma as a structural obstacle, the report notes scientists avoid topics 'like extraterrestrial technosignatures, which could damage their scientific credibility and promotion potential,' and finds 'public engagement in the effort to better understand UAP will be vital. NASA, by lending its name to UAP studies, is already helping to reduce stigma associated' with the subject.

HRR Volume I lists the 'UAP Independent Study Team (UAPIST) (June 2022-September 2023)' as one of the USG UAP investigatory efforts it catalogues, which is what puts a NASA civilian panel inside a Department historical record.

edges.label: Civil-agency complement to the DoD-led resolution office
edges.note: The Independent Study Team positioned NASA's expertise as supporting AARO within a 'whole-of-government framework', while acknowledging that much of the relevant military and intelligence data is classified.

edges.label: NASA chartered and published the Independent Study Team report
edges.note: The 16-member panel reported on 14 September 2023 with findings on data curation, satellite assets and the classification obstacle.

edges.label: Both hold analytical capability that could resolve material claims and neither has been tasked publicly
edges.note: NASA's report identifies the classification of military and intelligence data as the binding constraint; DOE laboratories hold the analytical instruments actually used by AARO. Reasoning: the capability exists and the tasking does not.

edges.label: Announced the appointment of a NASA Director of UAP Research
edges.note: In the report foreword Fox, Associate Administrator for the Science Mission Directorate, wrote that 'NASA is appointing a Director of UAP Research to centralize communications'.
